practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Lodhi Dynasty, which was the first Afghan ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi founded the Lodhi Dynasty in 1451 AD after displacing the last Sayyid ruler, Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah. He established the first Afghan ruling house in India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Behlul Lodhi ascend the throne of Delhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi ascended the throne of Delhi in 1451 AD, marking the transition of power from the Sayyid dynasty to the Lodhi dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: To which specific tribe of Afghans did Behlul Lodhi belong?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi belonged to the Shahu Khel branch of the Lodhi tribe, which was a prominent sub-division of the Pashtun/Afghan race settled in northern India. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which important regional kingdom was annexed by Behlul Lodhi and integrated into the Delhi Sultanate after a protracted conflict?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi fought a prolonged war against Hussain Shah Sharqi of Jaunpur and ultimately annexed the Sharqi kingdom to the Delhi Sultanate around 1479 AD. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the special copper coin introduced or circulated during the reign of Behlul Lodhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi introduced a copper coin known as 'Bahluli', which remained popular in northern India for a long time due to its high circulation and commercial utility. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Before becoming the Sultan of Delhi, Behlul Lodhi served as the governor of which strategic province?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi was the powerful governor of Sirhind during the reign of the Sayyid dynasty, utilizing this base to consolidate Afghan military power before capturing Delhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the last ruler of the Sayyid Dynasty whom Behlul Lodhi peacefully succeeded (by taking over Delhi)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah voluntarily abdicated the throne of Delhi in favor of Behlul Lodhi and retired to Badaun, enabling Behlul to take over peacefully. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the official royal court language during the Lodhi dynasty, including Behlul Lodhi's tenure?
practiceQuestions.sol: Although the Lodhis were of Afghan (Pashtun) origin, Persian continued to be the official language of administration, court records, and literature in the Delhi Sultanate. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who succeeded Behlul Lodhi upon his death in 1489 AD?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi was succeeded by his capable son Nizam Khan, who assumed the regnal title of Sikandar Lodhi in 1489 AD. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Approximately how long did Behlul Lodhi rule the Delhi Sultanate?
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi had a long and relatively stable reign of 38 years from 1451 AD until his death in 1489 AD. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes Behlul Lodhi’s political philosophy and his treatment of Afghan nobles?
opts: Absolute monarchy based on divine right, treating nobles as mere servants.
Tribal confederacy based on equality and sharing of power ('Kingship without sovereignty' / first among equals).
Absolute centralization where the Sultan personally managed all provincial revenue collection.
Theocratic governance strictly dictated by Ulema jurisprudence with no tribal autonomy.
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi based his rule on Afghan tribal traditions of equality. He did not sit on a high throne nor demand absolute subservience, preferring to be styled as 'first among equals' (Maglis-i-Sadaarat). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Behlul Lodhi manage the internal distribution of territories and revenue among his Afghan clansmen to maintain stability?
opts: By abolishing all jagirs and centralizing revenue under royal officers.
By distributing vast Iqtas/jagirs among Afghan nobles and relatives, treating the kingdom as joint property.
By handing over all administrative posts exclusively to foreign Persian and Turkish nobility.
By implementing a strict hereditary caste-based revenue farming system.
practiceQuestions.sol: To keep his fierce Afghan chieftains satisfied, Behlul Lodhi parcelled out the kingdom into various Iqtas (jagirs) distributed among his clan members, which prevented major internal rebellions but weakened central royal authority. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the historical significance of Behlul Lodhi’s conquest of the Sharqi Kingdom of Jaunpur?
opts: It ended a major geopolitical rival that had challenged Delhi's supremacy for decades and re-established Sultanate borders in the east.
It opened direct maritime trade routes with Southeast Asia through the Bay of Bengal.
It forced the ruler of Jaunpur to convert to Islam and pay heavy annual tributes without annexation.
It marked the complete elimination of Turkish influence from northern India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The annexation of Jaunpur eliminated Delhi's most persistent rival in the east, consolidated the Gangetic plain under the Lodhis, and expanded the territorial and economic base of the Sultanate. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Behlul Lodhi's approach towards his nobles differ fundamentally from that of subsequent sultans like Ibrahim Lodhi?
opts: Behlul respected noble autonomy and used persuasion, whereas Ibrahim treated nobles with harsh authoritarianism.
Behlul executed any noble who questioned his orders, while Ibrahim instituted a democratic council of ministers.
Behlul relied exclusively on foreign mercenaries, while Ibrahim trusted only local Hindu chiefs.
There was no difference; both practiced extreme despotic centralization.
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul understood the proud Afghan temperament and treated his nobles as peers. In contrast, Ibrahim Lodhi demanded absolute submission, causing deep alienation and revolts among the Afghan nobility. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the impact of Behlul Lodhi's economic measures and coin introductions on trade?
opts: They caused massive hyperinflation due to debasement of currency.
The introduction of stable copper 'Bahluli' coins facilitated local commerce and retail transactions.
Paper currency was introduced for the first time in North India.
Foreign trade was completely banned to promote domestic self-sufficiency.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bahluli copper coin became extremely popular for medium and small transactions, bridging the gap in the monetary system and boosting commercial exchanges across northern India. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the rise of the Lodhi Dynasty alter the ethnic composition of the ruling elite in the Delhi Sultanate?
opts: It replaced Turkish and Khalji dominance with an Afghan (Pashtun) nobility.
It brought Mongols directly into central administrative posts.
It completely excluded Muslims from power and appointed only Rajput chieftains.
It established a purely Arab ruling class modeled on the early Caliphates.
practiceQuestions.sol: Prior to the Lodhis, the Delhi Sultanate was dominated by Turks, Persians, and Khaljis. Behlul Lodhi inaugurated the First Afghan Empire in India, bringing Pashtun clans to the apex of political power. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was Behlul Lodhi's military strategy when facing numerically superior or entrenched enemies like the Sharqis?
opts: Employing guerrilla tactics, mobile cavalry maneuvers, and rallying Afghan reinforcements from tribal homelands.
Using elephant-only charges to break enemy formations instantly.
Avoiding all direct military engagements and relying solely on financial bribery.
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul Lodhi was a veteran commander who utilized flexible cavalry tactics, persistence, and continuous mobilization of Afghan fighters from trans-Indus regions to wear down opponents like the Sharqis. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best characterizes the relationship between Behlul Lodhi and the local Hindu population and zamindars?
opts: Systematic forced conversions and destruction of all temples throughout the kingdom.
Pragmatic accommodation of Hindu zamindars and local chiefs to ensure stable revenue collection and administrative functioning.
Total exclusion of Hindus from agricultural land ownership.
Appointment of Hindu nobles to high ministerial positions in Delhi.
practiceQuestions.sol: Like most pragmatic Sultans, Behlul Lodhi maintained working relations with local Hindu zamindars and chieftains, recognizing their crucial role in agricultural production and local revenue extraction. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Lodhi period often called a period of architectural transition rather than monumental grandeur?
opts: Because all construction was completely banned due to continuous famines.
Because architectural focus shifted towards functional garden tombs and fortress-palaces with sloping walls reflecting Afghan martial taste.
Because builders relied exclusively on wooden structures instead of stone.
Because builders completely abandoned Islamic dome architecture in favor of Hindu temple pillars.
practiceQuestions.sol: Lodhi architecture, developing further under Sikandar and Ibrahim, is noted for double domes, garden tombs (like Lodi Gardens), and sloping walls (batth), reflecting a blend of utility and martial aesthetics. [Primary Reference: An Introduction to Indian Art, NCERT Class 11]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the main systemic weakness inherited by the successors of Behlul Lodhi from his governance model?
opts: Excessive centralization leading to bureaucratic stagnation.
Decentralization of power to powerful Afghan clans who expected equality, making the Sultan vulnerable when centralization was attempted later.
Over-reliance on foreign mercenary armies from Central Asia.
Total bankruptcy of the royal treasury due to excessive spending on arts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Behlul's policy of treating nobles as equals and distributing large jagirs created powerful regional chieftains. When his successors tried to curb their autonomy, it sparked severe rebellions. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the foundation of the Lodhi Dynasty:
1. The Lodhi dynasty represents the first Afghan ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. Behlul Lodhi came to power by violently overthrowing the last Khilji sultan in 1451 AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Lodhis were Pashtuns/Afghans, making it the first Afghan dynasty of Delhi. Statement 2 is incorrect: Behlul Lodhi did not overthrow a Khilji sultan; rather, he succeeded the last Sayyid ruler (Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah) peacefully in 1451 AD. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Behlul Lodhi's administrative and political style:
1. He maintained the traditional Turkish concept of absolute divine monarchy and royal despotism.
2. He treated his Afghan nobles as peers and sat on a carpet in court instead of a lofty throne.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Behlul rejected Turkish despotism in favor of an Afghan tribal confederacy model. Statement 2 is correct: To emphasize equality among Afghan chieftains, he refused to sit on a throne and sat on a carpet with his nobles. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military campaigns of Behlul Lodhi:
1. He successfully annexed the independent Sharqi Kingdom of Jaunpur after a prolonged conflict.
2. He launched successful invasions across the Himalayas into Tibet and captured Lhasa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Behlul defeated Hussain Shah Sharqi and incorporated Jaunpur into Delhi Sultanate. Statement 2 is completely absurd and historically false; Delhi Sultanate rulers never invaded Tibet. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the coinage and currency during Behlul Lodhi's reign:
1. He introduced a copper coin called 'Bahluli' which gained immense popularity in northern India.
2. Gold coins were completely abolished and replaced entirely by cowrie shells during his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Bahluli copper coin was widely used in commercial transactions. Statement 2 is false; gold and silver currency continued alongside copper coins in trade and did not get replaced by cowries. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the tribal character of the Lodhi Dynasty:
1. The Lodhis belonged to the Pashtun race and encouraged immigration of Afghan tribesmen into India.
2. This immigration restricted military recruitment exclusively to non-Afghan mercenaries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Behlul encouraged Afghan tribesmen to migrate to India, offering them land and high positions. Statement 2 is incorrect because military recruitment was heavily centered around these newly arrived Afghan tribesmen, not non-Afghan mercenaries. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Behlul Lodhi's succession and descendants:
1. Behlul Lodhi was immediately succeeded upon his death in 1489 AD by his son Nizam Khan, who took the title Sikandar Lodhi.
2. Ibrahim Lodhi was the direct successor and son of Behlul Lodhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Nizam Khan (Sikandar Lodhi) succeeded Behlul in 1489 AD. Statement 2 is incorrect because Ibrahim Lodhi was the son of Sikandar Lodhi, making him the grandson of Behlul Lodhi, not his direct son. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the political relations between Delhi and provincial kingdoms during Behlul Lodhi's reign:
1. Behlul Lodhi successfully brought Mewat, Sambhal, and Gwalior into tributary relationships or direct control.
2. The Sultanate under Behlul remained restricted only to Delhi and Punjab without any southern or eastern expansion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Behlul forced several local chiefs and rulers in Mewat, Sambhal, Kol, and Gwalior to submit and pay tribute. Statement 2 is incorrect because he significantly expanded eastwards by conquering Jaunpur. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding historical sources on Behlul Lodhi:
1. Contemporary or near-contemporary chronicles such as 'Tarikh-i-Daudi' and 'Tarikh-i-Shahi' provide valuable insights into the Lodhi era.
2. Ibn Battuta's 'Rihla' is the primary historical text detailing the administrative reforms of Behlul Lodhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Works like 'Tarikh-i-Daudi' (by Abdullah) and 'Tarikh-i-Shahi' (by Ahmad Yadgar) are primary Afghan-period chronicles. Statement 2 is incorrect because Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the 14th century, long before Behlul Lodhi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative decentralization under Behlul Lodhi:
1. Behlul assigned large jagirs and administrative units to his kinsmen and Afghan nobles to secure their loyalty.
2. This system successfully prevented any future conflicts between the Sultan and his nobles during the entire Lodhi dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Behlul distributed jagirs among his kinsmen to satisfy clan ambitions. Statement 2 is incorrect because later under Ibrahim Lodhi, this very autonomy of the nobles led to severe civil strife and defections (such as Daulat Khan Lodhi inviting Babur). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Lodhi dynasty with the preceding Delhi Sultanate dynasties:
1. While previous dynasties like the Tughlaqs and Khaljis were dominated by Turco-Persian elites, the Lodhis represented a distinct Pashtun (Afghan) tribal polity.
2. The Lodhi Sultans adopted the Persian title 'Zill-i-Ilahi' (Shadow of God) and maintained strict court etiquette like 'Sijda' and 'Paibas'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Lodhis marked the advent of Afghan political hegemony in India. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Lodhis rejected despotic Persian court customs like Sijda (prostration) and Paibas (kissing the monarch's feet), adhering instead to egalitarian Afghan tribal traditions where nobles sat together with the Sultan. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]
